htn_kidney.abstract: Tubulointerstitial fibrosis and inflammation are hallmark pathological features of hypertensive nephropathy (HN), yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Zyxin, a focal adhesion protein, has been implicated in hypertension-related pathologies, but its specific role in HN-induced tubulointerstitial injury remains undefined. An HN murine model was established via a multi‑hit DOCA/Ang II + uninephrectomy + high salt approach. Intrarenal zyxin was overexpressed using adeno-associated virus. portal_hypertension.abstract: Background : There have been recent proposals to replace non-cirrhotic portal fibrosis (NCPF), idiopathic portal hypertension (IPH), idiopathic non-cirrhotic portal hypertension, nodular regenerative hyperplasia, etc. with an all-encompassing term "porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder." However, the Asia-Pacific Association for Study of the Liver recommended continued use of the term NCPF/IPH. Methods : We sent this questionnaire-based online survey to capture the clinical perspectives of 300 specialized experts in the Asia-Pacific region with complete anonymisation. portal_hypertension.abstract: Immune dysregulation in paediatric portal hypertension (PHT) is poorly understood. We aimed to characterise T cell phenotype and function and circulating immune mediators in children with PHT according to disease aetiology. Forty-four children with PHT (27 chronic liver disease [CLD]-related and 17 portal vein thrombosis [PVT]-related) and 15 healthy controls were prospectively enrolled. Peripheral and portal blood samples were analysed using multiparameter flow cytometry and ELISA to assess T cell subsets, chemokine receptors, cytokines and soluble immune markers. portal_hypertension.abstract: Splenic vein aneurysms (SVAs) are a rare vascular anomaly of the portal system that are often asymptomatic and found incidentally on imaging. Intervention is reserved for aneurysms that are enlarging, thrombosed, symptomatic, or ruptured to avoid catastrophic complications. This can range from endovascular to open, complex procedures. Here, we present the case of a massive, symptomatic, partially thrombosed SVA that required a hybrid approach involving both minimally invasive and open surgery. A 56-year-old woman presented to the emergency department for an infected right foot wound and was admitted for intravenous antibiotics and surgical debridement.
